requirement_text.REQ-029: Extend REQ-028's graph module with src/definition/graph.zig's validateNodeAttributes() (PD-05) and the edge-condition rules (PD-06). Edge condition rules (PD-06): condition MUST be present (non-null, non-empty) on every non-default outgoing edge from an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, MUST be null on every other edge; is_default MUST NOT coexist with a non-null condition; at most one outgoing edge per EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY may be default. Also port isValidCelSyntax's minimal structural CEL check as a pure syntax-only validator.

task.description: Design the fix for ISS-0056: CHK-14 (check_non_gateway_condition_absence/1) currently forbids any non-nil condition on any non-EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY-sourced edge, which blocks REQ-048's entire conditioned-task-completion feature on :HUMAN_TASK edges outright, not just the narrow multi-condition-no-fallback case ISS-0056 names. Design: (1) loosen CHK-14 to permit real conditions on :HUMAN_TASK-sourced edges, (2) add a new CHK check (verify next unused number yourself) requiring at least one fallback-candidate outgoing edge on a :HUMAN_TASK node whenever any outgoing edge is really-conditioned. Zero change to lib/letflow/engine/ permitted.
acceptance_criteria: Design covers loosening CHK-14 to permit :HUMAN_TASK-sourced conditions, with the exact new guard stated
Design covers the new CHK check (verified CHK number, exact violation code and message shape)
States exactly which existing function(s) change and how their guard changes, in prose/pseudocode-signature terms only, no implementation code
Confirms zero change required outside lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex and its test file
States edge cases considered, including the single-edge conditioned-non-default HUMAN_TASK case and CHK-13/16 precedent search
No implementation code (no .ex/.exs function bodies) anywhere in the design artefact

result.summary: Design artefact written at lib/letflow/design/iss-0056-human-task-fallback-edge-validation.md. Confirmed by direct grep of graph.ex that CHK-01..18 are taken (CHK-18 = check_sub_process_interface/1, REQ-032) so CHK-19 is the next free number, per ISSUE-FIXER's own suggestion, verified independently rather than trusted. Two changes designed, both confined to lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex: (1) a new private human_task_source?/3 helper (mirrors exclusive_gateway_source?/3's shape/defensive-dangling-source convention but checks :HUMAN_TASK), and check_non_gateway_condition_absence/1 (CHK-14) renamed to check_unpermitted_edge_condition/1 with its guard broadened to permit a non-nil condition when the source is either (a) an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with is_default != true (unchanged) or (b) a HUMAN_TASK (new, unconditional on is_default -- reasoned through in design doc SS3.3 why CHK-15 alone already correctly rejects the one invalid HUMAN_TASK is_default+condition combination, so no redundant carve-out is needed); violation code stays :unexpected_edge_condition, only the message text and trigger logic change. (2) A new CHK-19 check_human_task_fallback_edge/1, dispatched from validate_edge_conditions/1's existing check list (not validate_node_attributes/1's -- it's an edge-condition check, not a node-attribute one), firing :human_task_no_fallback_edge once per offending HUMAN_TASK node (not per edge) when at least one outgoing edge is really-conditioned and none is a fallback candidate. The 'really conditioned' predicate is deliberately mirrored literally from transition.ex's really_conditioned?/1 (is_default != true AND is_binary(condition) AND condition != "", no String.trim) rather than reusing graph.ex's own trim-aware blank_condition?/1 helper, per the diagnosis's explicit instruction to avoid future drift between the two modules -- this introduces a real, narrow semantic gap (a whitespace-only condition is 'really conditioned' under CHK-19 but 'blank' under CHK-17) which the design flags explicitly in SS4.1 as an open question, not silently resolved. SS6 works through 7 edge cases including the single-edge conditioned-non-default HUMAN_TASK case (fires, no precedent exists in CHK-13/16 for a fallback requirement at all -- confirmed by reading both, neither has an analogous concept) and the zero-outgoing-edge case (does not fire, CHK-04's territory). SS7 makes an explicit, reasoned decision NOT to extend CHK-16 to HUMAN_TASK sources in this run (ISSUE-FIXER flagged it optional/non-blocking; extending it would require a second non-trivial design decision about violation-counting semantics this design has no mandate to make on ISS-0056's authority alone), naming it as a candidate for a future separately-filed issue rather than silently dropping it. SS0 states the zero-change-outside-graph.ex confirmation explicitly and lists what must NOT change (SS8), including every existing CHK function this design leaves untouched. No .ex/.exs code blocks anywhere in the document -- all algorithm steps are @spec-level signatures or FOR/IF-shaped pseudocode, matching this project's iss-0048 design-doc convention. Acceptance-criteria traceability table (SS11) maps every handoff acceptance criterion to its concrete design section.
